items.detail:
The repair inserts the same ~55-word block verbatim into both pages: "One caveat for anyone running the same check: the router's endpoints API returns the model record with an empty `endpoints` array for this slug (HTTP 200, measured 2026-09-02), while the standard row still lists endpoints. Nothing published resolves whether that means the slug is aliased internally or genuinely unroutable; OpenRouter's notice, quoted above, is the authority that requests still route." The caveat itself is correct and I measured it true on both slugs, so this is not a factual objection — but two sibling entries carrying an identical paragraph is the uniform-block shape the voice bar exists to catch, and a reader who opens both in tabs sees copy-paste. Either reword one of the two so the sentence order and framing differ, or bind the shared half as a `{{fact:…}}`-style transclusion so the duplication is structural rather than authored.

items.detail:
The revised summary says GLM-5.3 stands "third on the card's own row (behind Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol)" — literally accurate, but the card's ExploitGym footnote reads "We evaluate GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3 and Qwen3.8 Max in Claude Code 2.1.207" and names TPS rescaling factors for exactly those three (115 / 40 / 47). It says nothing about where the Fable 5 (181/247), GPT-5.6 Sol (216/293) or Opus 4.8 (80/120) figures came from, or whether the same rescaled budget applies to them. So the ranking the summary now cedes is a comparison between a number Z.ai measured under a stated method and three numbers whose method the card does not state. Fix: when the post is written, add half a sentence to the evidence block saying the card states its ExploitGym method for GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max only — so the post inherits the asymmetry instead of presenting the row as one like-for-like leaderboard.
